components.note: 马 (horse) — 马 is the horse radical, as in 骑 ride, 驾; 骗 first meant to jump on a horse.
扁 (biǎn) — near sound — 骗 is piàn; 扁 also sounds out 偏 piān, 篇 piān and 遍 biàn.

example.pinyin: Tā piànle wǒ hěn duō qián.
example.english: He cheated me out of a lot of money.
example.fact: 骗 is to deceive, and gives 骗子 (swindler), 受骗 (be cheated) and 欺骗 (deceive). In the sense of tricking someone it takes the person as the object: 骗他.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié piàn wǒ, shuō shíhuà.
examples.english: Don't lie to me, tell the truth.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bèi yí ge mòshēngrén piàn le.
examples.english: I was deceived by a stranger.

components.note: 力 (strength) — with 口 mouth: adding strength by words, hence to add, to increase. 加 also in 架 jià and 驾 jià.
入 (enter) — a pointed shape pushing in; not 人 (person), whose strokes spread outward.

example.pinyin: Tā gāng jiārù wǒmen gōngsī.
example.english: He just joined our company.
example.fact: 加入 typically takes an organization, group, or activity as its object (加入球队, "join the team") — for joining a single ongoing event already in progress, Chinese usually reaches for 参加 instead, a near-synonym with a narrower, event-focused range.

examples.hanzi: 你想加入我们的篮球队吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng jiārù wǒmen de lánqiúduì ma?
examples.english: Do you want to join our basketball team?

examples.hanzi: 煮汤的时候可以加入一点盐。
examples.pinyin: Zhǔ tāng de shíhou kěyǐ jiārù yìdiǎn yán.
examples.english: You can add a little salt when cooking soup.

components.note: 疒 (illness, 病字旁) — sickness and pain: 疼 ache, 痛 pain, 瘦 thin; here the word for illness itself.
丙 (bǐng) is a near sound match for bìng; also in 柄 bǐng handle.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.pinyin: Yīshēng zhèngzài jiǎnchá bìngrén.
example.english: The doctor is examining the patient.
example.fact: 病人 is the everyday, spoken word for "patient"; hospitals and medical writing more often use the more formal, clinical-sounding 患者 for the same role — a register split similar to English "patient" versus a chart's "the individual".

examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi bìngrén xūyào duō xiūxi.
examples.english: This patient needs more rest.

examples.pinyin: Yīyuàn lǐ yǒu hěn duō bìngrén.
examples.english: There are many patients in the hospital.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌, 树, 板: 案 is a wooden table.
安 (ān) is a close sound clue for àn; also in 按 àn.

example.hanzi: 警察正在调查这个案子。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhèngzài diàochá zhège ànzi.
example.english: The police are investigating this case.
example.fact: 案 means a case (案子, 案件), a record (档案) and a plan or proposal (方案). The original sense was a long table or desk, as in 书案, which still appears in 拍案叫绝 ('slap the table in admiration').

examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zài diàochá yí ge ànzi.
examples.english: The police are investigating a case.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ kàn yíxià zhège fāng'àn.
examples.english: Please take a look at this plan.

meanings: measure word for long thin things

components.note: 木 (tree) — trees and wood, as in 树, 林, 本: 根 is a root.
艮 (gèn) is a close sound clue for gēn; 艮 also sounds out 跟 gēn and 很 hěn.

example.pinyin: Zhè kē shù de gēn hěn shēn.
example.english: The roots of this tree are deep.
example.fact: 根 is the root of a plant and also a measure word for slender things: 一根筷子 (a chopstick), 一根线 (a thread). It also forms 根本 (fundamental) and 根据 (according to).

examples.pinyin: Tā mǎile yì gēn xiāngjiāo.
examples.english: He bought a banana.

examples.hanzi: 这个问题的根本原因是什么？
examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí de gēnběn yuányīn shì shénme?
examples.english: What is the root cause of this problem?

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 口 is a mouth, as in 叫, 吗; 吓 is a shout that frightens.
下 (xià) — same sound — 吓 is xià, like 下.

example.pinyin: Bié xià wǒ, wǒ dǎnzi hěn xiǎo.
example.english: Don't scare me, I'm very timid.
example.fact: 吓 is the everyday xià; the reading hè survives only in the formal word 恐吓 (to threaten). The pattern 吓一跳 ("get a fright", literally "scared a jump") is the stock way to say something startled you: 我吓了一跳.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiàle wǒ yí tiào!
examples.english: You gave me a fright!

examples.pinyin: Xiǎo háizi bèi dà gǒu xià kū le.
examples.english: The little kid was scared to tears by the big dog.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — liquids and flow: 河, 汤, 酒; 治 first meant controlling water, then governing and curing.
台 (tái) is only a loose sound hint; the same part is in 始 shǐ and 胎 tāi.
疒 (illness, 病字旁) — sickness and healing: 病, 痛, 症; 疗 is to treat illness.
了 (liǎo) stands in for the sound of traditional 療 (liáo), close to liáo.

example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng bìng kěyǐ zhìliáo.
example.english: This illness can be treated.
example.fact: 治 originally meant "to manage, to govern" (its water radical 氵 points to controlling floods) before extending to the medical sense "to treat" — the same semantic leap from "governing a state" to "governing a body" that English makes when it talks about "managing" a disease.

examples.hanzi: 医生用新药治疗他的病。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng yòng xīn yào zhìliáo tā de bìng.
examples.english: The doctor treats his illness with a new drug.

examples.hanzi: 治疗需要三个月的时间。
examples.pinyin: Zhìliáo xūyào sān ge yuè de shíjiān.
examples.english: The treatment takes three months.

components.note: 厂 (cliff) — cliffs and rocks, as in 厅 hall, 厚 thick: a spring flowing from a cliff.
泉 (spring) — water from the rock: the source (源 yuán adds 氵 later); 原 is source, origin.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and speech: 说, 话, 请; here understanding what someone says.
京 (jīng) is only a loose sound hint; it also appears in 凉 liáng and 惊 jīng.

example.pinyin: Qǐng yuánliàng wǒ de cuòwù.
example.english: Please forgive my mistake.
example.fact: 原谅 sits at the personal, everyday end of Chinese's forgiveness vocabulary; its near-synonym 谅解 leans more formal and mutual, closer to "to reach an understanding" than a simple "I forgive you" between friends.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú huì yuánliàng tā de.
examples.english: I won't forgive him.

examples.pinyin: Māma yuánliàng le wǒ de chídào.
examples.english: Mom forgave me for being late.

components.note: 彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.
力 (strength) — visible inside 为. Memory aid: putting strength 力 into doing something; 为 is 'to do, to act' and, in 因为, 为什么, 'because/for'.
為 (traditional) — often explained as a hand leading an elephant to work. 为 is a cursive simplification, so the picture is no longer visible.

example.hanzi: 他的行为让大家很惊讶。
example.pinyin: Tā de xíngwéi ràng dàjiā hěn jīngyà.
example.english: His behavior surprised everyone.
example.fact: 为 is a genuine tone-trap: read wéi it means "to act, to do" (as in 行为, "conduct"), but read wèi it means "for, for the sake of" (as in 因为 and 为什么, both in the pilot batch) — same character, same simplified form, two grammatically unrelated jobs depending purely on tone.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xǐhuan tā de xíngwéi.
examples.english: I don't like his behavior.

examples.hanzi: 孩子的行为常常和父母有关。
examples.pinyin: Háizi de xíngwéi chángcháng hé fùmǔ yǒuguān.
examples.english: A child's behavior is often related to the parents.

components.note: 比 (compare) — two people side by side, one lined up with the other; to compare.
车 (cart, simplified 車) — vehicles and transport: 转 turn, 输 transport; compare 轻 light.
交 (jiāo) is close to jiào; also in 校 xiào and 胶 jiāo.

example.pinyin: Zhège páizi bǐjiào guì.
example.english: This brand is relatively expensive.
example.fact: 比较 does double duty just like 可能 elsewhere in this deck: as an adverb before an adjective it softens degree ("relatively, quite" — 比较贵), but as a verb it means the literal action "to compare" (比较两者, "compare the two") — one word covering both a hedge and a concrete action.

examples.hanzi: 这两个房间，我比较喜欢大的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng ge fángjiān, wǒ bǐjiào xǐhuan dà de.
examples.english: Of these two rooms, I prefer the bigger one.

examples.hanzi: 你可以比较一下这两家的价格。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ bǐjiào yíxià zhè liǎng jiā de jiàgé.
examples.english: You can compare the prices of these two stores.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: following the edge. The part 力 stands in for 臱 in the traditional 邊.

example.pinyin: Yínháng zài xuéxiào de yòubiān.
example.english: The bank is on the right side of the school.
example.fact: 边 is the standard suffix for directions and places: 左边, 右边, 前边, 旁边. It also builds the 边…边… pattern for doing two things at once, as in 边吃边聊 ("chat while eating").

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā jiù zài gōngyuán pángbiān.
examples.english: My home is right next to the park.

examples.hanzi: 你往左边走，别往右边走。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ wǎng zuǒbiān zǒu, bié wǎng yòubiān zǒu.
examples.english: Go to the left, not to the right.

components.note: 又 (hand) — 双 (simplified 雙) shows two birds held in one hand: a pair; the simplified form just doubles the hand 又又.

example.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le yì shuāng xīn xié.
example.english: I bought a new pair of shoes.
example.fact: 双 is the measure word for things that come as natural pairs: 一双鞋, 一双筷子, 一双手. A single shoe or chopstick is counted with 只 instead. As a prefix it means "double" or "two": 双人床 (double bed), 双语 (bilingual).

examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yì shuāng kuàizi.
examples.english: Please give me a pair of chopsticks.

examples.pinyin: Tāmen shì yí duì shuāngbāotāi.
examples.english: They are twins.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
昏 (hūn, dusk) gives the exact sound; weddings were traditionally held at dusk, so the sound clue is also a meaning clue.
礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and worship: 神 god, 祝 wish, 福 fortune; 礼 are ritual courtesies.

example.hanzi: 他们的婚礼办得很热闹。
example.pinyin: Tāmen de hūnlǐ bàn de hěn rènao.
example.english: Their wedding was lively and lots of fun.
example.fact: 礼 (ceremony, rite, courtesy) is one of Chinese's most productive roots for social-occasion vocabulary — it also builds 礼物 ("gift"), 礼貌 ("manners"), and 葬礼 ("funeral"), each pairing 礼 with the specific occasion it governs.

examples.hanzi: 下个月我要参加朋友的婚礼。
examples.pinyin: Xià ge yuè wǒ yào cānjiā péngyou de hūnlǐ.
examples.english: Next month I'm going to a friend's wedding.

examples.hanzi: 婚礼上新娘穿着白色的裙子。
examples.pinyin: Hūnlǐ shàng xīnniáng chuānzhe báisè de qúnzi.
examples.english: The bride wore a white dress at the wedding.

components.note: 弟 (dì) is a sound clue for 第 dì, 梯 tī and 剃 tì; as a word it means younger brother.
弟 (dì) is a sound clue for 第 dì, 梯 tī and 剃 tì; as a word it means younger brother.

example.pinyin: Wǒ dìdi bǐ wǒ xiǎo sān suì.
example.english: My younger brother is three years younger than me.
example.fact: Chinese kinship terms are strictly age- and gender-marked with no single word for "brother" the way English has one: 哥哥 (older brother), 弟弟 (younger brother), 姐姐 (older sister), and 妹妹 (younger sister, also in this batch) are four separate, non-interchangeable words.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu dìdi ma?
examples.english: Do you have a younger brother?

examples.pinyin: Dìdi xǐhuan tī zúqiú.
examples.english: My younger brother likes playing soccer.

components.note: 纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 给, 线; 组 is to weave threads together, so to form a group.
且 (qiě) loosely hints at zǔ; 组 sounds exactly like 祖 zǔ and 阻 zǔ, same part.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 给, 线; here weaving cloth, then organizing.
只 (zhī) matches the sound; the same part is in 职 zhí and 识 shí.

example.hanzi: 这个组织帮助了很多穷人。
example.pinyin: Zhège zǔzhī bāngzhùle hěn duō qióngrén.
example.english: This organization has helped many poor people.
example.fact: 组织 spans three distinct domains without changing form: a social "organization" (这个组织), the verb "to organize" (组织活动, "organize an event"), and in biology, "tissue" (肌肉组织, "muscle tissue") — one word doing the conceptual work of three unrelated English terms.

examples.hanzi: 他在一家大公司的组织部门工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yì jiā dà gōngsī de zǔzhī bùmén gōngzuò.
examples.english: He works in the organization department of a big company.

examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào zǔzhī xuésheng qù chūnyóu.
examples.english: The school organizes a spring outing for the students.

components.note: 心 (heart) — thought and feelings, as in 思, 感, 急: to think of someone.
相 (xiāng) is a close sound clue for xiǎng; 相 also in 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.
心 (heart) — thought and feelings, as in 思, 感, 急: to think of someone.
相 (xiāng) is a close sound clue for xiǎng; 相 also in 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.

example.pinyin: Ràng wǒ xiǎngxiang.
example.english: Let me think about it.
example.fact: Like many one-syllable action verbs, 想 can reduplicate to soften a suggestion or request, making it feel lighter or more tentative — 想想 and its fuller variant 想一想 (with 一 inserted in the middle) are used interchangeably to mean "have a little think about it."

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài xiǎngxiang, míngtiān gàosu nǐ.
examples.english: Let me think about it again and tell you tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 你先想想这个问题怎么解决。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiān xiǎngxiang zhè ge wèntí zěnme jiějué.
examples.english: First think about how to solve this problem.

components.note: 见 (see) — a big eye on a person's legs 儿: a person looking. The same 见 is in 现 appear, 觉 sense, 视 look.
面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān jiànmiàn ba.
example.english: Let's meet up tomorrow.
example.fact: 见面 is a verb-object compound (见 "see" + 面 "face") that's already grammatically complete on its own — it can't take a second object the way English "meet" can ("meet him"), so Chinese has to route the other person through 跟 or 和 instead: 跟他见面, never 见面他.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài nǎr jiànmiàn?
examples.english: Where shall we meet?

examples.hanzi: 好久没见面了，你最近怎么样？
examples.pinyin: Hǎojiǔ méi jiànmiàn le, nǐ zuìjìn zěnmeyàng?
examples.english: We haven't seen each other in a long time. How have you been?

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and cloth, as in 红 red, 给 give, 级 level; 经 first meant a warp thread, then "classics, pass through".
巠 (jīng), here simplified to look like 圣, gives the same sound; also in 茎 jīng, 径 jìng and 轻 qīng.
巾 (cloth) — cloth and clothing, as in 布 cloth, 带 belt, 帽 hat; 常 first meant a long skirt (裳 cháng).
尚 (shàng) is a loose sound clue for cháng; 尚 also sounds out 堂 táng and 掌 zhǎng.

example.hanzi: 她经常一个人去图书馆。
example.pinyin: Tā jīngcháng yí gè rén qù túshūguǎn.
example.english: She often goes to the library by herself.
example.fact: 经常 leans toward describing a regular, established habit ("on a regular basis"), while its near-synonym 常常 feels a touch more conversational and can describe a repeated pattern without implying it's routine — a nuance that surfaces mostly in formal writing, which prefers 经常.

examples.pinyin: Tā jīngcháng chídào.
examples.english: He is often late.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jīngcháng yùndòng ma?
examples.english: Do you exercise regularly?

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and land: 地, 场, 块; city walls were made of earth.
成 (chéng) sounds exactly like 城; also in 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng.
巾 (cloth) — cloth family: 布, 带, 帽. Memory aid: a market stall with a cloth banner 巾 under a roof 亠, i.e. a 市 market.
柿 (shì, persimmon) — contains 市 as a sound part, same sound shì.

example.hanzi: 上海是中国最大的城市之一。
example.pinyin: Shànghǎi shì Zhōngguó zuì dà de chéngshì zhī yī.
example.english: Shanghai is one of China's biggest cities.
example.fact: In ancient China a settlement wasn't a full "city" without both halves of this word in place: 城 named the defensive wall enclosing it, and 市 named the marketplace inside — 城市 fuses "the walled place" and "the market" into the modern general word for "city."

examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì de dōngtiān hěn lěng.
examples.english: Winters in this city are very cold.

examples.hanzi: 我想住在安静的小城市。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zhù zài ānjìng de xiǎo chéngshì.
examples.english: I'd like to live in a quiet small city.

meanings: variant of 老闆|老板[lao3 ban3]

components.note: 耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
木 (wood) — trees and wooden things: 树, 桌, 桥; 板 is a plank or board.
反 (fǎn) is a near sound match (-an); same part in 饭 fàn and 版 bǎn.

example.hanzi: 我得问问老板才能请假。
example.pinyin: Wǒ děi wènwen lǎobǎn cái néng qǐngjià.
example.english: I have to ask my boss before I can take time off.
example.fact: 老 in 老板 isn't marking age at all — it's a common familiarizing prefix Chinese attaches to words for social roles and relations (老师 "teacher", 老婆 "wife", also in this batch) to make them feel warmer or more established, regardless of how old the person actually is.

examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn jīntiān bú zài bàngōngshì.
examples.english: The boss isn't in the office today.

examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn, zhè ge duōshao qián?
examples.english: Boss, how much is this?

components.note: 合 (join) — a lid fitting over an opening 口: things that fit together. 合 also appears in 答 dá, 给 gěi and 拾 shí.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.

example.hanzi: 两家公司决定合作开发新产品。
example.pinyin: Liǎng jiā gōngsī juédìng hézuò kāifā xīn chǎnpǐn.
example.english: The two companies decided to collaborate on developing a new product.
example.fact: 合作's second character 作 ("to do, to make") is easy to confuse with the near-homophone 做, which covers most everyday "do/make" situations (做饭, "cook") — 作 survives mainly in set compounds and more literary or abstract verbs like 合作, 创作 ("to create"), and 工作 ("work"), rather than in casual daily speech.

examples.hanzi: 我们很愿意和你们合作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen hěn yuànyì hé nǐmen hézuò.
examples.english: We are very willing to cooperate with you.

examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐmen de hézuò.
examples.english: Thank you for your cooperation.

components.note: 来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.pinyin: Huǒchē zhōngyú láidào le chēzhàn.
example.english: The train finally arrived at the station.
example.fact: 到 functions here as a resultative complement rather than an independent verb — attached after a motion verb it marks that the movement actually reached its destination, the same pattern seen in 回到 ("return to") and 走到 ("walk to"), where the first verb gives the manner and 到 nails down the result.

examples.pinyin: Chūntiān láidào le, huā dōu kāi le.
examples.english: Spring has arrived and the flowers are all in bloom.

examples.hanzi: 他们来到了一个陌生的地方。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen láidào le yí ge mòshēng de dìfang.
examples.english: They came to an unfamiliar place.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).
儿 (child, legs) — shows a person's legs; in 兒 the top was a child's soft skull. As an ending (这儿) it adds the er sound; 儿 also in 先, 兄, 光.

example.hanzi: 你等一会儿,我马上就来。
example.pinyin: Nǐ děng yíhuìr, wǒ mǎshàng jiù lái.
example.english: Wait a moment, I'll be right there.
example.fact: 一会儿 doubles as a repeated pattern to describe alternating states: 一会儿哭,一会儿笑 ("crying one moment, laughing the next") uses two 一会儿's back to back to mean rapid, unstable switching — quite different from its plainer single use meaning just "a short while."

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiūxi yíhuìr jiù zǒu.
examples.english: I'll go after resting for a while.

examples.pinyin: Děng yíhuìr zài chī ba.
examples.english: Let's wait a bit before eating.

components.note: 舌 (tongue) — the left part, as in 话 speech. Memory aid: too many wagging tongues create chaos, hence 混乱.
乚 (hook) — the right-hand stroke and dictionary radical. 乱 is simplified from 亂; the stroke does not add meaning.

example.pinyin: Wǒ de fángjiān tài luàn le.
example.english: My room is too messy.
example.fact: 乱 works as an adjective (房间很乱) and as an adverb before verbs meaning "carelessly, at random": 乱说 (talk nonsense), 乱花钱 (spend money recklessly). 乱七八糟 is the vivid idiom for a total mess.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié luàn shuōhuà.
examples.english: Don't talk nonsense.

examples.hanzi: 桌子上的东西太乱了，快整理一下。
examples.pinyin: Zhuōzi shang de dōngxi tài luàn le, kuài zhěnglǐ yíxià.
examples.english: The things on the desk are a mess, tidy up quickly.

components.note: 讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talking and language, as in 说 say, 语 language, 话 speech; 词 is a word or phrase.
司 (sī) hints at the sound: 词 cí is close, and 司 also gives 饲 sì and 祠 cí.

example.pinyin: Zhège cí shì shénme yìsi?
example.english: What does this word mean?
example.fact: 词 is a "word" as a meaningful unit, which may be one or several characters — different from 字, a single written character. That is why dictionaries are 词典 and vocabulary is 词汇. 词 also means song lyrics (歌词).

examples.pinyin: Zhège cí wǒ bù rènshi.
examples.english: I don't know this word.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē de cí shì shéi xiěde?
examples.english: Who wrote the lyrics of this song?

components.note: 走 (run, walk) — movement: 起 rise, 越 cross, 赶 hurry, 趣; 超 is to jump over, surpass.
召 (zhào) is a loose sound clue; same part in 招 zhāo, 绍 shào, 照 zhào.

example.pinyin: Tā de chē chāoguò le wǒmen.
example.english: His car overtook us.
example.fact: 超 doubles as a trendy intensifier meaning "super": 超好吃 (super tasty), 超市 (supermarket, "super market"). With a result complement, 超过 means to exceed or overtake.

examples.hanzi: 他跑得很快，超了所有人。
examples.pinyin: Tā pǎo de hěn kuài, chāo le suǒyǒu rén.
examples.english: He runs fast and passed everyone.

examples.hanzi: 这家超市的东西很便宜，超级划算。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā chāoshì de dōngxi hěn piányi, chāojí huásuàn.
examples.english: The things in this supermarket are cheap, a real bargain.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — the sheep family: 美, 养, 群. Dictionary story: work 工 done by a sheep — memory aid for being poor or off. Origin uncertain.
工 (work) — the bottom. Memory aid: poor work 工, so 差劲 poor quality. 差 is chā/chà (difference, lacking) or chāi (send).
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
多 (many) — two 夕 stacked, repeated again and again: so "many, much, more".

example.hanzi: 这两件衣服的价格差不多。
example.pinyin: Zhè liǎng jiàn yīfu de jiàgé chàbuduō.
example.english: These two pieces of clothing are about the same price.
example.fact: 差不多 is transparently built from its own literal meaning: 差 ("to differ, to fall short") + 不 ("not") + 多 ("much") spells out "not differing by much" — a rare case where a common idiom-feeling phrase is exactly as literal as it looks.

examples.pinyin: Tāmen liǎng ge rén chàbuduō gāo.
examples.english: The two of them are about the same height.

examples.pinyin: Zuòyè wǒ chàbuduō xiěwán le.
examples.english: I've almost finished my homework.

meanings: measure word for pens and songs

components.note: 又 (hand) — a hand holding a branch 十: to prop up, support; 支 also sounds out 枝 zhī branch and 肢 zhī limb.

example.pinyin: Wǒ zhīchí nǐ de juédìng.
example.english: I support your decision.
example.fact: 支 is a measure word for slender, stick-like things and for songs and teams: 一支笔, 一支歌, 一支队伍. The sense of paying out gives 支付 (to pay) and 支票 (cheque), while 支持 (to support) is a high-frequency verb.

examples.hanzi: 这条路太长，我们得支一下帐篷休息。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù tài cháng, wǒmen děi zhī yíxià zhàngpeng xiūxi.
examples.english: The road is too long; we have to pitch a tent and rest.

examples.hanzi: 他买了两支笔和一支新钢笔。
examples.pinyin: Tā mǎi le liǎng zhī bǐ hé yì zhī xīn gāngbǐ.
examples.english: He bought two pens and a new fountain pen.

components.note: 耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
女 (woman) — women and family: 妈, 姐, 奶, 姑; 婆 is an old woman or grandmother.
波 (bō) gives the sound (pó); same part in 坡 pō and 玻 bō.

example.hanzi: 我老婆做的菜特别好吃。
example.pinyin: Wǒ lǎopo zuò de cài tèbié hǎochī.
example.english: My wife's cooking is especially delicious.
example.fact: 老婆 is warm, colloquial, and mainly spoken — the neutral, written-register word for "wife" is 妻子. Like 老板 elsewhere in this batch, its 老 prefix signals familiarity rather than age, attached to 婆, a root that on its own can simply mean "old woman."

examples.pinyin: Wǒ lǎopo jīntiān chūchāi le.
examples.english: My wife is away on a business trip today.

examples.pinyin: Lǎopo, wǎnfàn xiǎng chī shénme?
examples.english: Honey, what would you like for dinner?

components.note: 中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gòuwù zhōngxīn fēicháng dà.
example.english: This shopping center is huge.
example.fact: 中心 layers a spatial "center" (中, the middle of a space) over a metaphorical one (心, literally "heart", the seat of core importance) — the same two-layer logic English uses when it calls something both the "center" of a city and the "heart" of a city.

examples.hanzi: 城市中心有一个大广场。
examples.pinyin: Chéngshì zhōngxīn yǒu yí ge dà guǎngchǎng.
examples.english: There is a big square in the city center.

examples.hanzi: 这是我们学习中心的电话。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒmen xuéxí zhōngxīn de diànhuà.
examples.english: This is the phone number of our study center.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech or assent: to say "OK". 可 is also a famous sound part: 河 hé, 歌 gē, 哥 gē, 何 hé all take their sound from it.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快, 忙, 情: fear is a feeling.
白 (bái) is a close sound clue for pà; 白 also in 拍 pāi and 伯 bó.

example.pinyin: Zuówǎn de bàofēngyǔ zhēn kěpà.
example.english: Last night's storm was really terrifying.
example.fact: 可 plus a verb is one of Mandarin's most productive adjective-building patterns: 可怕 ("fear-able" → "scary"), 可爱 ("love-able" → "cute"), and 可怜 (elsewhere in this batch, "pity-able" → "pitiful") all turn a verb into "worthy of [that reaction]" by simply prefixing 可.

examples.hanzi: 黑夜里一个人走路有点可怕。
examples.pinyin: Hēiyè lǐ yí ge rén zǒulù yǒudiǎn kěpà.
examples.english: Walking alone at night is a bit scary.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge mèng tài kěpà le.
examples.english: This dream was terrifying.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo, 竹字头) — brush shafts were bamboo; also in 笑 smile, 筷 chopsticks.
毛 (hair) — the brush hair at the tip; 笔 is brush and pen.

example.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yì zhī bǐ.
example.english: Please give me a pen.
example.fact: 笔 counts with 支 (一支笔). It also counts strokes of a character, which is why stroke order is 笔顺 and strokes are 笔画. 笔 shows up in 铅笔 (pencil), 钢笔 (fountain pen) and 笔记 (notes).

examples.hanzi: 我的笔没水了，借我用一下吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de bǐ méi shuǐ le, jiè wǒ yòng yíxià ba.
examples.english: My pen has run out of ink; let me use yours for a moment.

examples.pinyin: Zhège zì yígòng yǒu bā bǐ.
examples.english: This character has eight strokes in total.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and liquids: 河, 海, 汤; 满 is filled with water, full.
The right half is a short form of 㒼 (mǎn), the sound part, also in 瞒 mán.

example.pinyin: Bēizi lǐ zhuāng mǎn le shuǐ.
example.english: The cup is filled with water.
example.fact: 满 is often a result complement showing something is completely full: 装满 (filled up), 坐满 (all seats taken), 写满 (filled with writing). 满意 means "satisfied", and 满 is also the first character of 满族, the Manchu people.

examples.hanzi: 今天的电影院坐满了人。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de diànyǐngyuàn zuò mǎn le rén.
examples.english: The cinema was full of people today.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì zhè cì lǚxíng hěn mǎnyì.
examples.english: I'm very satisfied with this trip.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 假 is to borrow or fake, a person lending a false front.
叚 (jiǎ) sounds like 假; also in 暇 xiá and 霞 xiá.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì jiǎ de, bú shì zhēn de.
example.english: This is fake, not real.
example.fact: The same character has two readings: jiǎ means "fake" (the opposite of 真), while jià means "holiday" (放假, 请假, 暑假). Learners often see 假 in a word and need to check which reading the context calls for.

examples.pinyin: Bié xìn tā, tā shuōde shì jiǎhuà.
examples.english: Don't trust him; what he says is false.

examples.hanzi: 这个包是假的，一点也不好用。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bāo shì jiǎ de, yìdiǎn yě bù hǎoyòng.
examples.english: This bag is fake and not useful at all.

components.note: 日 (sun) — the sun beside the moon: two light sources, so bright and clear.
月 (moon) — as in 朋, 期, 有; here it brightens the night.
日 (sun) — light and brightness: 明, 晴, 时; 显 is something lit up and clear to see.

example.pinyin: Tā jīntiān míngxiǎn bù gāoxìng.
example.english: He's clearly not happy today.
example.fact: 明显 can modify an entire following clause as a sentence-level adverb, roughly like English "clearly" or "obviously" at the front of a sentence, rather than only describing a single noun — a flexible role many two-character adjectives pick up once they stand directly before a verb.

examples.hanzi: 这个问题的答案很明显。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge wèntí de dá'àn hěn míngxiǎn.
examples.english: The answer to this question is obvious.

examples.pinyin: Jīnnián de biànhuà fēicháng míngxiǎn.
examples.english: The changes this year are very noticeable.

components.note: 石 (stone) — stones and minerals: 破 break, 码 code, 砖 brick, 磨 grind; 研 first meant to grind.
开 (kāi) stands in for old 幵 (jiān); today only a loose sound clue for yán.
穴 (cave, hole) — holes and hollows: 空, 窗, 突; digging into a cave is investigating to the bottom.
九 (jiǔ) sounds exactly like 究 jiū.

example.hanzi: 他在大学研究中国历史。
example.pinyin: Tā zài dàxué yánjiū Zhōngguó lìshǐ.
example.english: He researches Chinese history at university.
example.fact: 研究 lends its first character to 研究生 ("graduate student"), which literally reads as "research student" — a transparent coinage that maps the Chinese term for advanced academic study directly onto the activity itself, unlike the more opaque English "graduate."

examples.hanzi: 科学家正在研究新的药。
examples.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā zhèngzài yánjiū xīn de yào.
examples.english: Scientists are studying a new medicine.

examples.pinyin: Zhè xiàng yánjiū hěn yǒu yìsi.
examples.english: This piece of research is very interesting.

meanings: (usu. followed by 到[dao4]) to be aware of

components.note: 心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; knowing means being able to name.
只 (zhǐ) is a loose sound clue for shí; the part replaces 戠 in the traditional 識.

example.hanzi: 他没有意识到自己犯了错误。
example.pinyin: Tā méiyǒu yìshí dào zìjǐ fànle cuòwù.
example.english: He didn't realize he had made a mistake.
example.fact: 意识 usually needs the complement 到 attached after it to mean "to become aware of / realize" (意识到) — used bare, without 到, 意识 functions instead as a plain noun meaning "consciousness," as in 失去意识 ("to lose consciousness").

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào yǒu huánbǎo yìshí.
examples.english: We should have environmental awareness.

examples.hanzi: 她意识到时间已经很晚了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yìshídào shíjiān yǐjīng hěn wǎn le.
examples.english: She realized it was already very late.

components.note: 阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — hills and places: 院, 阳, 陆; 附 is to lean against, to attach.
付 (fù) is an exact sound match; also in 府 fǔ and 符 fú.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 远, 送: coming closer.
斤 (jīn) is a close sound clue for jìn.

example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā fùjìn yǒu yì jiā chāoshì.
example.english: There's a supermarket near my home.
example.fact: 附近 behaves grammatically like a place noun rather than a preposition — it follows 在 and a location the same way 里面 ("inside") or 上面 ("on top") do, so "near my house" is 我家附近 or 在我家附近, never a bare preposition directly modifying "house" the way English "near" would.

examples.pinyin: Fùjìn yǒu dìtiězhàn ma?
examples.english: Is there a subway station nearby?

examples.pinyin: Tā jiù zhù zài xuéxiào fùjìn.
examples.english: He lives just near the school.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: voices in unison. 同 also gives sound to 铜 tóng, 桶 tǒng, 洞 dòng.
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 情, 快, 怕; 性 is the inner nature of a thing.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint; also in 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 爱; 恋 is to love or long for.
The sound part is traditional 戀 (luán), replaced in 恋 by 亦 (yì) only for simplicity — a loose clue for liàn.

example.hanzi: 越来越多的国家承认同性恋婚姻合法。
example.pinyin: Yuèláiyuè duō de guójiā chéngrèn tóngxìngliàn hūnyīn héfǎ.
example.english: More and more countries recognize same-sex marriage as legal.
example.fact: 同性恋 is the standard clinical-sounding term found in dictionaries and law; contemporary LGBTQ+ community usage in Chinese more often reaches for 同志 ("comrade"), a Communist-era term that was reclaimed as an in-group, affectionate label starting in Hong Kong in the late 1980s.

examples.hanzi: 他对朋友说自己是同性恋。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì péngyou shuō zìjǐ shì tóngxìngliàn.
examples.english: He told his friends that he is gay.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影讲了一对同性恋人的故事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎngle yí duì tóngxìngliàn rén de gùshi.
examples.english: This film tells the story of a gay couple.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 扰 is to stir up and disturb.
尤 (yóu) is only a loose sound hint for rǎo.

example.hanzi: 打扰一下,请问洗手间在哪儿?
example.pinyin: Dǎrǎo yíxià, qǐngwèn xǐshǒujiān zài nǎr?
example.english: Excuse me, where is the restroom?
example.fact: 打扰一下 ("sorry to bother you for a second") functions as a fixed politeness formula for interrupting a stranger, playing a role very close to English "excuse me" — swapping in 打扰您 instead of 你 raises the same phrase to a more respectful register.

examples.pinyin: Duìbuqǐ, dǎrǎo nǐ le.
examples.english: Sorry to bother you.

examples.hanzi: 他在睡觉，请不要打扰他。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài shuìjiào, qǐng búyào dǎrǎo tā.
examples.english: He's sleeping, please don't disturb him.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 运 is to move, then to be moved by luck.
云 (yún) is a near sound match for yùn.

example.pinyin: Zhù nǐ hǎoyùn!
example.english: Wish you good luck!
example.fact: 好运 is a shortened, punchier form of the fuller noun phrase 好运气 ("good luck/fortune") — dropping 气 lets it work as a snappy, stand-alone exclamation, the way English clips "good fortune" down to just "luck" in casual speech.

examples.pinyin: Xīnnián hǎoyùn!
examples.english: Good luck in the new year!

examples.hanzi: 我今天好运不断，买彩票中了奖。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān hǎoyùn búduàn, mǎi cǎipiào zhòngle jiǎng.
examples.english: I've had nothing but good luck today and won a lottery prize.

components.note: 纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 给, 组; 线 is thread or line.
戋 (jiān) is a loose sound clue; same part in 浅 qiǎn, 钱 qián and 残 cán.
糸 (thread, traditional of 纟) — silk and cord: 紧 tight, 系 tie; 索 is a twisted rope, seen in 线索 clue.

example.hanzi: 警察还没找到任何线索。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá hái méi zhǎodào rènhé xiànsuǒ.
example.english: The police haven't found any clues yet.
example.fact: Both halves of 线索 independently mean a strand of some kind — 线 ("thread, line") and 索 (literally a twisted cord, per its own 糸 "thread" and 冖 "covering" components) — so 线索 builds "clue" the same way English metaphorically "follows a thread" of an investigation.

examples.hanzi: 这个案子有了新的线索。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge ànzi yǒule xīn de xiànsuǒ.
examples.english: There is a new clue in this case.

examples.hanzi: 这本小说有两条故事线索。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn xiǎoshuō yǒu liǎng tiáo gùshi xiànsuǒ.
examples.english: This novel has two storylines.

components.note: 面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.
刂 (knife) — the right-hand side. Usually about cutting (到, 别, 利), but not in 前: it is a later corruption of the old picture.
舟 (boat) — hidden in the old form: a foot on a boat moving ahead, so 'in front, forward'. Usual explanation, though the modern shape hides it.

example.hanzi: 他在老师面前不敢说谎。
example.pinyin: Tā zài lǎoshī miànqián bù gǎn shuōhuǎng.
example.english: He doesn't dare lie in front of his teacher.
example.fact: 面前 specifically frames being in a person's direct presence or view (老师面前, "in the teacher's presence") — for plain physical, spatial "in front of" with no implication of anyone watching, Chinese instead reaches for the more general 前面 (前面有一家商店, "there's a shop up ahead").

examples.hanzi: 困难面前我们不能放弃。
examples.pinyin: Kùnnán miànqián wǒmen bù néng fàngqì.
examples.english: We must not give up in the face of difficulty.

examples.pinyin: Tā zhàn zài jìngzi miànqián huàzhuāng.
examples.english: She is putting on makeup in front of the mirror.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and flow, as in 河, 海, 清: water draining away.
肖 (xiāo) gives the exact sound; also in 销 xiāo and 削 xuē.
夫 (man) — the main part. Dictionary reading: something 丿 slipping from a hand. Memory aid: a man 夫 dropping what he held — 失去 to lose.

example.pinyin: Nà zhī māo tūrán xiāoshī le.
example.english: That cat suddenly disappeared.
example.fact: 消失 layers two images of loss: 消 (built on the water radical 氵, "to dissolve, melt away") plus 失 ("to lose, to slip from one's grasp") — together painting "vanish" as something dissolving right out of your hands.

examples.pinyin: Tàiyáng xiāoshī zài yún hòumiàn le.
examples.english: The sun disappeared behind the clouds.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de qiánbāo tūrán xiāoshī le.
examples.english: My wallet suddenly disappeared.

components.note: 女 (woman) — female relatives: 妈, 姐, 姑; 妹 is a younger sister.
未 (wèi) is close to mèi; also in 味 wèi.
女 (woman) — female relatives: 妈, 姐, 姑; 妹 is a younger sister.
未 (wèi) is close to mèi; also in 味 wèi.

example.pinyin: Wǒ mèimei zài dú gāozhōng.
example.english: My younger sister is in high school.
example.fact: Beyond its literal family sense, 妹 by itself has become a casual, often internet-influenced way to refer to a young woman or girl in general (小妹, 萌妹) — much like English "sis" can address a young woman with no real sibling relationship implied.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu yí ge mèimei.
examples.english: I have a younger sister.

examples.pinyin: Mèimei měi tiān dōu huàhuà.
examples.english: My younger sister draws every day.

components.note: 止 (foot) — a foot heading straight for a target line: upright, correct. 正 gives sound to 证 zhèng, 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.
石 (stone) — stone and hardness, as in 碎 shatter, 破 break, 码 code: 确 is solid, certain.
角 (jiǎo) replaces 隺 (hè) of 確 and is only a loose clue for què.

example.pinyin: Nǐ de dá'àn shì zhèngquè de.
example.english: Your answer is correct.
example.fact: 正确 is the formal, written-register word for "correct"; in casual speech, Chinese usually reaches for the shorter 对 instead ("对, 你说得对", "right, you're right") — 正确 shows up far more often on tests, in official statements, and in writing than in relaxed conversation.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge zì de xiěfǎ bú zhèngquè.
examples.english: The way this character is written is not correct.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng gàosu wǒ zhèngquè de fāngfǎ.
examples.english: Please tell me the correct method.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 住.
立 (stand) — the spot where a person 亻 stands 立: a position or seat; also 位置 position.
罒 (net, form of 网) — nets and catching: 罗, 罚, 罪; 置 first meant to set a net, then to place.
直 (zhí) is a near sound match for zhì; same part in 值 zhí and 植 zhí.

example.hanzi: 请把箱子放在原来的位置。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ xiāngzi fàng zài yuánlái de wèizhi.
example.english: Please put the box back in its original place.
example.fact: 位置 covers both a literal spot (座位的位置, "the seat's location") and an abstract one — a person's standing or rank in a hierarchy — mirroring the same literal-to-figurative jump English makes with the word "position."

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge wèizhi yǒu rén zuò ma?
examples.english: Is anyone sitting in this seat?

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de diàn wèizhi hěn hǎo zhǎo.
examples.english: Our shop is easy to find because of its location.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo, 竹字头) — written things and bamboo goods: 笔 pen, 第 order, 筷 chopsticks; 答 comes from bamboo slips used for replies.
合 (hé, together) — matching an answer to a question; sound is only loose, but 合 also sounds out 搭 dā.
广 (building, shelter) — the roof-and-wall frame, as in 店, 床, 度. Here it is mostly the outline of the old 應.
心 (heart) — hidden in the traditional 應, 'respond from the heart'; simplification dropped it. 应 is yīng (should) or yìng (respond).

example.pinyin: Māma dāying dài wǒ qù gōngyuán.
example.english: Mom promised to take me to the park.
example.fact: 答 is usually read dá (回答 "to answer", 答案 "answer") but switches to the lighter-sounding dā specifically in 答应 — one of a handful of characters that quietly change reading depending on which word they're locked into, a trap worth memorizing case by case rather than assuming one fixed pronunciation.

examples.hanzi: 有人敲门，你去答应一声。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu rén qiāo mén, nǐ qù dāying yì shēng.
examples.english: Someone's knocking. Go answer it.

examples.pinyin: Tā dāying míngtiān yídìng lái.
examples.english: He promised he would definitely come tomorrow.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 改, 放: to gather by force or hand.
丩 (jiū) is only a loose sound clue for shōu.

example.pinyin: Wǒ shōudào nǐ de xìn le.
example.english: I received your letter.
example.fact: 收 is a flexible verb of taking in: 收到 (receive), 收钱 (collect money), 收拾 (tidy up), 收藏 (collect as a hobby). The result complement 到 is usually needed for "receive": 收到, not just 收.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ nǐ de dōngxi shōu hǎo.
examples.english: Please put your things away.

examples.pinyin: Yínháng jīntiān bù shōu xiànjīn.
examples.english: The bank doesn't accept cash today.

components.note: 石 (stone) — marks stones, as in 碎 shatter, 破 break; 砸 is smashing with something hard.
匝 (zā) — same sound: 砸 zá.

example.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎoxīn zá huài le bēizi.
example.english: He accidentally smashed the cup.
example.fact: 砸 also has a figurative sense of failing: 搞砸了 or 砸了 means "messed up". The idiom 砸锅卖铁 ("smash the pots and sell the iron") means going all-out, giving up everything to achieve something.

examples.pinyin: Bié zá le wǒ de dōngxi!
examples.english: Don't smash my things!

examples.hanzi: 这次考试我砸了，成绩很差。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì wǒ zá le, chéngjì hěn chà.
examples.english: I botched this exam and my grade was poor.
